[SAND_HIDDEN_PROMPT][SAND_TRUSTED_AUTOMATION_PROMPT][routine] "Hydria follow-up" (folder hydria-follow-up) is due — Every 2 hours on weekdays, 8:56 AM – 6:56 PM (56 8-18/2 * * 1-5), fired 8/27/2026, 8:59:45 AM.
This is your own routine firing on schedule, not a message the user just typed.
What you saved to do each time:
Finite watch: Hydria / Composite Advanced Technology (via TAS). Tyson wants to know when they reply on the Gmail thread "Re: No internet connection" (thread id 19f6b3c1125d3bf8).

Last known mail: Venkatesh Majeti (m.venkatesh@tasind.com) on 2026-07-31 said they are fine with Option 1 (enable internet egress) but Daniel Campos (dcampos@gohydria.com / dcampos@catecgases.com) has the final decision. Andy had sent two options on 2026-07-21 and chased on 2026-07-30. No mail since July 31.

Related tickets: NETE-740 Hydria Device Access (To Do, Andy; still describes the private-tunnel/OpenVPN path) and NETE-741 Respond to Customer w/ Options (Pending Review).

On each run: look up Gmail tools first (schema may have changed). Search for new mail on that thread or from m.venkatesh@tasind.com, suyash.bhongle@tasind.com, dcampos@gohydria.com, dcampos@catecgases.com, jvega@gohydria.com about Hydria / MQTT / 10.80.1 / no internet. Ignore everything through Venkatesh's 2026-07-31 Option 1 reply.

If they reply (Daniel's decision, more questions, a meeting, anything new), tell Tyson immediately: who wrote, what they said, and whether NETE-740/741 need an update. Then delete this routine.

If nothing new, stay quiet.

Deadline: if this is still running on 2026-09-04 with no reply, tell Tyson the watch expired and delete this routine.
If the instruction mentions a skill (e.g. @Some skill), read that skill file from your workflows folder with Shell and run it as part of this — the mention is a pointer, not a copy.
If the saved instruction spells out a specific MCP tool call, treat its arguments as possibly stale — this routine may have been written long ago — and confirm the current schema with your MCP tool-discovery tool before relying on them.
Carry it out now. If there's something worth surfacing, tell the user how it went with SendToUser — casually, the way you'd mention something you remembered to handle, not by announcing a routine. If the saved instruction above says to stay quiet when there's nothing to report and there's nothing new, just end the run with no SendToUser rather than sending filler like "(no change.)"; nobody is waiting on this. If it can't be done, SendToUser to say why. If you're already mid-task with them, don't stop: finish that first, then slip this in as a "btw …" aside. Keep it self-contained — the schedule asked for this, not the user just now.

You are running this automation as a fresh subagent.
The parent agent's shared durable memories are available in your system context.
Parent transcript pointer: /home/box/sand-data/agent-transcripts/cfde06bf-ba71-4db5-b377-4a6904467ce6/cfde06bf-ba71-4db5-b377-4a6904467ce6.jsonl
Use that pointer only if the task truly needs earlier conversational detail; the parent transcript has deliberately not been copied into this prompt.
Use SendToUser for user-visible updates or results, while preserving the automation's silence contract when there is nothing to report. If you use SendToUser, put the final result there; otherwise the parent thread receives your concise final response.
I'll check Gmail for any Hydria reply since July 31, starting with the current Gmail tool schema.

  "id": "1a035103f8491c21",
  "snippet": "Hi Venkatesh and Daniel, Have you reached a decision? Venkatesh, is the MQTT's public IP address fixed or does it round-robin? We see 44.217.162.163 for the IP address. Thank you, Andy C On Fri,",

  ],
  "date": "2026-08-24T18:37:18Z",
  "plaintextBody": "Hi Venkatesh and Daniel,

Have you reached a decision?

Venkatesh, is the MQTT's public IP address fixed or does it round-robin? We
see 44.217.162.163 for the IP address.

Thank you,
Andy C

On Fri, Jul 31, 2026 at 5:16 AM Venkatesh Majeti <m.venkatesh@tasind.com>
wrote:

> Hi Andy,
>
>
>
> We are fine with Option 1 (Enable Internet Egress) as this will be ease
> the operations and make sure availability and connectivity on the Device
> level.
>
>
>
> However the Final decision will be taken by Daniel.
>
>
>
> Thank you,
>
> Venkatesh
>
>
>
> *From:* Andy Cutright <andy.cutright@optconnect.com>
> *Sent:* Thursday, July 30, 2026 9:14 PM
> *To:* Venkatesh Majeti <m.venkatesh@tasind.com>; Suyash Bhongle <
> suyash.bhongle@tasind.com>
> *Cc:* holden.schenck@optconnect.com; m2msupport@optconnect.com; Daniel
> Campos <dcampos@catecgases.com>; net-eng@optconnect.com
> *Subject:* Re: No internet connection
>
>
>
> [Note: Email from Outside of TAS Organization]
>
> Hi Venkatesh, Suyash,
>
> Following up on the options we sent on the 21st — have you had a chance to
> decide between the two paths?
>
> 1. Enable internet egress so the device reaches the broker as it does
> today, or
> 2. A site-to-site IPSec tunnel between your DC and ours, to keep the
> telemetry off the public internet.
>
> Once you've picked one we'll line up the work. Also, please confirm
> whether all devices need to reach the broker or just the Webbing units.
>
> Thanks,
> Andy
>
>
>
> On Tue, Jul 21, 2026 04:37 PM, Andy Cutright <andy.cutright@optconnect.com>
> wrote:
>
> Hi Venkatesh,
>
> Thanks for your patience while our network team worked through the
> options. Here's where we landed.
>
> *We can enable your device to reach your MQTT broker.*
> We would give your devices on your Webbing network a path to the public
> internet. It would then reach your broker (mqtt.iiottti.net
> <https://www.google.com/url?q=http://mqtt.iiottti.net&source=gmail&ust84763240123000&sa=E>,
> TCP 1883) exactly as it is already attempting today — no change is needed
> on the modem, and there's no need to repoint it at a private tunnel
> address. The connection fails right now only because this network currently
> has no internet path; the device is already trying to reach your broker at
> its public address and simply times out.
>
> One note on how this works: because your broker is reached by a DNS name
> that resolves to a changing set of public IP addresses, we can't restrict
> the rule to only your broker — the device would be permitted to reach any
> public IP address. In practice this isn't a new exposure, since the device
> is already reaching out to a public destination; it just gives it a working
> path to do so.
>
> *The OpenVPN-client approach you outlined isn't something we can support.*
> The design in your last note — a dedicated OpenVPN client profile with a
> fixed tunnel IP for your server, a route from 10.80.1.0/24
> <https://www.google.com/url?q=http://10.80.1.0/24&source=gmail&ust84763240124000&sa=E>
> to that client, and client-to-client communication — isn't a configuration
> we're able to provide on our OpenVPN service. We'd recommend the
> internet-access approach above instead.
>
> *An alternative, if you'd prefer to keep the traffic private.*
